eyebrow: Two numbers, same date -- don't assume which is wrong
code:
-- Finance's legacy query, point-in-time, 9/30
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) FROM memberships
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' ...;
-- 41,920

-- member_activity_mart, any day in September
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM member_activity_mart
WHERE activity_month = '2026-09-01'
  AND was_active_any_day;
-- 43,588
caption: Two different questions, not two different answers to the same one.

eyebrow: Same grain Finance used -- exact match
code:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM int_active_members
WHERE activity_date = '2026-09-30'
  AND is_active;
-- 41,920  -- matches Finance exactly
caption: The headcount mismatch is closed. The business logic is correct.

eyebrow: But the report has a dollar figure right next to it
code:
SELECT SUM(amount_paid_usd) FROM stg_billing
WHERE date_trunc('month', billing_period_start)
      = '2026-09-01';
-- $1,285,340

SELECT SUM(total_revenue_usd) FROM revenue_mart
WHERE revenue_month = '2026-09-01';
-- $37,966,830   <- ~29.5x higher
caption: A spot-checked invoice shows exactly why: one $49 charge, matching 30 rows.
